transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I came in today because... well, I know the people at my apartment building are watching my comings and goings. They keep tabs on me, and they're slipping notes about me down to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices being put on the doors, but... I know what's actually happening.

Besides these beliefs about being watched, have you noticed any recent changes in your mood, such as feeling unusually elated, irritable, or full of energy, or on the other hand feeling very down, hopeless, or losing interest in things?

I definitely haven't been full of energy or elated, no. It's... well, it's more the other way around. I have been feeling really down lately. Most mornings, I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's just like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor.
Did the feeling that people were watching you and leaving notes about you start around the same time as your low mood, or were you noticing that before you started feeling this down?

Well, it's... they kind of go together, I guess. I mean, when I'm really down in that hollow place, you know, when I'm barely eating or even answering the phone... that's when I'm the most sure that the people in the building are tracking me and talking to the office about me. It just all seems to happen at the same time.
Have there been times when your mood felt more normal or less heavy, and if so, did you still feel that people in your building were watching you and reporting on you during those times?

Yeah, there was a time. I had a spell of several weeks where I was actually eating a bit better, and... well, I wasn't waking up feeling so hopeless every single day. The heavy feeling lifted a bit. But even during those weeks, I still knew the neighbors were watching my door. I still knew they were reporting on me to the office. That part didn't stop just because my mood was a little better.
Have you had earlier periods in the past—separate from this current one—where you felt this same kind of deep, hollow depression for weeks at a time, with your mood returning to normal in between?

Well, it doesn't really go back to normal in between. Honestly, for most of the time since I moved into this place... it's just been like this. 

Even on the days when I could maybe think a bit better and sound a little clearer, I still felt really low. Just... useless, I guess. I haven't been interested in any of the things I used to do for a long time now. So, yeah, that heavy feeling hasn't really gone away, it's been there for the majority of the time since I moved.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient endorses persistent persecutory delusions (belief that neighbors are surveilling and reporting on her) that have continued essentially unchanged even during a several-week period when her depressive symptoms (hollow mood, anhedonia, hopelessness, appetite/social withdrawal) partially remitted. This demonstrates that psychotic symptoms occur independent of, and outside the duration of, the mood episode, ruling out MDD with psychotic features (where psychosis should only occur during mood episodes). However, mood symptoms have also been present for the majority of the illness course since moving into the apartment, which argues against a primary psychotic disorder like schizophrenia (where mood symptoms would be brief/incidental). The concurrent presence of a major depressive syndrome with psychotic symptoms both during and outside the mood episoande, over a substantial duration, is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, depressive type, unspecified (F25.9).
